# Glossary {.unnumbered #sec-glossary}

::: {.audience}
For everyone
:::

The words this guide uses, in plain terms, with the chapter that explains
each one. Chapters not written yet are given by number.

[Adjustment]{#adjustment}
:   A movement that corrects stock outside a count, with a reason, such as a
    piece damaged and sent for melting. See @sec-ledger.

[Approver]{#approver}
:   A person who can open a count's Review and complete it, but only for a
    count they didn't count in. See @sec-counting.

[Audit trail]{#audit-trail}
:   The unbroken record of every change to the stock: what changed, when, why
    and who entered it. Mistakes are corrected with new entries, never
    erased. See @sec-ledger.

[Below zero]{#below-zero}
:   Stock the ledger says is less than none. It always means a movement is
    missing or wrong, such as a sale entered before its delivery. See
    @sec-ledger.

[Blind count]{#blind-count}
:   A count in which the counters never see what the ledger expects, so they
    count what is there rather than what should be. See @sec-counting.

[Book stock, the books]{#book-stock}
:   The shop's billing system's own record of what is in stock. Jholok can
    load it into a count. Chapter 11.

[Box photo]{#box-photo}
:   A photo of a box of cards, from which Jholok proposes how many of each
    product are in it. Chapter 9.

[Card]{#card}
:   The small card each pair of earrings or each set sits on in a box.
    Jholok's box photos count cards, not loose pieces. Chapter 9.

[Cost]{#cost}
:   What the shop paid for one piece of a product, with the metal, the making
    charge and any stones. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Count]{#count}
:   Finding what is really in the shop and comparing it with what the ledger
    expects. Also called a stock take. See @sec-counting.

[Count adjustment]{#count-adjustment}
:   The movement Jholok records when an approver completes a count and accepts
    a difference. See @sec-counting.

[Counter]{#counter}
:   A person who counts. Counters count blind, and submit the count for
    review. See @sec-counting.

[Cover]{#cover}
:   How long a product's stock lasts at the pace it has sold recently. See
    @sec-stock-basics.

[Crore (Cr)]{#crore}
:   One hundred lakh: ₹1,00,00,000. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Cut-off]{#cut-off}
:   The moment a count line's expected stock is taken from, so that sales
    during a count don't look like losses. Chapter 12.

[Difference, discrepancy]{#discrepancy}
:   When counted and expected don't agree: short or over. See @sec-counting.

[Expected]{#expected}
:   What the ledger says should be in the shop. Counters never see it while
    counting. See @sec-counting.

[Jangad]{#jangad}
:   Stock sent out of the shop on approval, with a memo, for a customer or
    another jeweller to see. It is still the shop's stock until it is sold.
    Chapter 12.

[Karigar]{#karigar}
:   The craftsman who makes or repairs jewellery for the shop. Stock with the
    karigar is still the shop's. Chapter 12.

[Lakh (L)]{#lakh}
:   ₹1,00,000. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Ledger]{#ledger}
:   The record of every movement of stock, oldest first. See @sec-ledger.

[List price]{#list-price}
:   What the shop asks a customer for one piece of a product. See
    @sec-stock-basics.

[Making charge]{#making-charge}
:   What it costs to make a piece, on top of the metal. Part of a product's
    cost. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Matched]{#matched}
:   A product whose count agrees with what was expected. See @sec-counting.

[Memo]{#memo}
:   The numbered slip that goes with stock sent out on jangad. Chapter 12.

[Movement]{#movement}
:   One change to a product's stock: opening stock, received, sold, returned,
    an adjustment or a count adjustment, and a few more. See @sec-ledger.

[Odd single]{#odd-single}
:   A single earring found without its pair. Jholok marks it and never rounds
    it into a pair. See @sec-stock-basics.

[On hand, stock on hand]{#on-hand}
:   How many of a product the shop has: the sum of all its movements. See
    @sec-stock-basics and @sec-ledger.

[Opening stock]{#opening-stock}
:   The stock a product already had when it was added to Jholok. See
    @sec-ledger.

[Order]{#order}
:   Stock set aside for a customer's order. It is not on the shelf, but it is
    still the shop's. Chapter 12.

[Over]{#over}
:   More found than expected. Often a delivery or a return that wasn't
    entered. See @sec-counting.

[Owner]{#owner}
:   The person who runs the shop in Jholok. The owner sets up the people,
    proves it's them for exports and backups, and can approve a count. Chapter
    4.

[Pair]{#pair}
:   Two matching earrings, counted and sold as one. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Piece]{#piece}
:   The unit for everything that isn't earrings or a set: a ring, a chain, a
    coin. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Piece tag]{#piece-tag}
:   A code on one individual piece, different from every other piece's. It
    links to its product through the tag list. Chapter 5.

[PIN]{#pin}
:   The short number each person enters to show who they are. An approver's
    PIN is their signature on a completed count. Chapter 4.

[Product]{#product}
:   One design in one metal and weight, so that every piece of it is alike.
    See @sec-stock-basics.

[Reconciliation]{#reconciliation}
:   Comparing what was counted with what was expected, and explaining every
    difference. See @sec-counting.

[Recount]{#recount}
:   Counting a product again. A shortage must be recounted, blind, before it
    can be accepted. See @sec-counting.

[Review]{#review}
:   The screen where an approver sees the counted and expected numbers side
    by side, and decides which differences to accept. See @sec-counting.

[Separation of duties]{#separation-of-duties}
:   Making sure the person who counts isn't the person who approves, so no one
    can hide a loss alone. See @sec-counting.

[Set]{#set}
:   Pieces sold together as one, such as a necklace with matching earrings.
    Counted as 1. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Short]{#short}
:   Fewer found than expected. Recounted before it is accepted. See
    @sec-counting.

[Shrinkage]{#shrinkage}
:   Stock lost without being sold: theft, damage or mistakes. See
    @sec-counting.

[SKU]{#sku}
:   *Stock keeping unit*: a product's own short code, such as EAR-0002. See
    @sec-stock-basics.

[Stock]{#stock}
:   The jewellery the shop owns and means to sell. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Stock value]{#stock-value}
:   What the stock is worth: each product's stock on hand times its cost, or
    its list price, added up. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Tag list]{#tag-list}
:   The list linking each piece tag to its product, imported from a
    spreadsheet or linked in the app. Chapter 5.

[Type]{#type}
:   A group of products, such as Earrings or Rings. A type sets the unit its
    products are counted in. See @sec-stock-basics.

[Unit]{#unit}
:   What a type is counted in: pairs, sets or pieces. Different units are never
    added together. See @sec-stock-basics.
